title: BSOD triggered when AlwaysOnTop module is enabled, especially around display sleep/reconfiguration
author: MickyLangello
summary: The reporter correlates repeated display sleep, wake, lock, or monitor power changes with a repeatable win32kbase stack-recursion BSOD while Always On Top is enabled, and has supplied a replacement diagnostic archive after the initial archive was rejected.

judgment.rationale: The report provides an actionable module, environment, control condition, repeatable display-state sequence, and kernel failure signature. The author has now supplied a replacement archive and the issue is marked Needs-Team-Response, so a maintainer should reproduce on a current build before selecting a code fix.
evidence: The reporter describes three matching UNEXPECTED_KERNEL_MODE_TRAP (0x7F) double-fault dumps with recursion in win32kbase!vUnreferencePdevWorker.
The reported trigger is repeated sleep/wake, lock/display timeout, or monitor power cycling with two 1440p 180Hz DisplayPort displays while Always On Top is enabled.
The reporter says recurrence stopped after disabling Always On Top while other PowerToys modules remained enabled.
A replacement PowerToys report archive was attached in a new author comment on 2026-09-03, and the live labels changed from Needs-Author-Feedback to Needs-Team-Response.
Recent history for AlwaysOnTop.cpp includes a WM_ENDSESSION shutdown-hang fix, but no focused fix for this display-stack kernel recursion.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the display reconfiguration scenario on a current build with Always On Top alternately enabled and disabled, then use the resulting logs and crash signature to determine whether a safe PowerToys-side mitigation is possible.

fix_assessment.rationale: A PowerToys-side mitigation may be applicable if current-build reproduction confirms that Always On Top's display-related window-event activity triggers the kernel recursion. No linked PR or other existing fix currently covers the reported failure.

proposed_fixes.title: Isolate and mitigate Always On Top activity during display reconfiguration
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Unconfirmed hypothesis: Always On Top window-event activity during repeated display topology changes contributes to a win32k display-object lifetime recursion on the affected Windows and graphics configuration. The kernel stack trace and module-disable control establish correlation, not a PowerToys user-mode root cause.
plan: Reproduce the reported display sleep/wake or monitor power-cycle sequence on a current build with Always On Top enabled and disabled as paired control runs.
Correlate the replacement diagnostic archive and any reproduction logs with Always On Top's display-related event handling to identify a specific user-mode operation preceding the failure.
If a repeatable PowerToys operation is identified, make the smallest scoped change to suppress, defer, or safely reinitialize that operation during display reconfiguration.
Add focused regression coverage where the isolated event boundary is testable and retain manual multi-monitor validation for the display-stack scenario.
verification: Run repeated sleep/wake, lock/display-timeout, and single-monitor power-cycle scenarios on a multi-monitor system with Always On Top enabled and disabled.
Confirm no recurrence of the reported 0x7F failure and that normal pin, unpin, and foreground-window behavior continue to work.
Validate the change on a current stable Windows build before treating an older OS or graphics-stack interaction as a PowerToys defect.

confidence.rationale: The reproduction boundary and control condition are unusually specific, but the kernel-mode fault does not identify a PowerToys call site and the replacement archive has not yet been analyzed.

issue_context.summary: A display-state transition stress scenario is reported to trigger a repeatable kernel stack-recursion BSOD only while Always On Top is enabled; the reporter has now supplied a replacement diagnostic archive.
known_information: The original report used PowerToys 0.100.2 on Windows 11 24H2 build 26100 with two 1440p 180Hz DisplayPort displays.
The report names repeated sleep/wake, monitor power cycling, and lock/display timeout as triggers.
Three dumps reportedly share the 0x7F double-fault and win32kbase PDEV recursion signature.
The reporter says disabling Always On Top stopped recurrence while other listed PowerToys modules remained enabled.
The first archive was rejected, but the author supplied a replacement archive on 2026-09-03.
There is no assignee, linked issue, linked PR, or existing fix associated with this report.
inferences: Always On Top may be a trigger during display reconfiguration, but the kernel stack does not establish that its code is the root cause.
A current-build control reproduction can distinguish a stale version-specific interaction from an ongoing module interaction.
issue_context.analysis: The updated author evidence and Needs-Team-Response label mean this should no longer remain in an author-waiting state. The report is sufficiently detailed for a maintainer-controlled reproduction, while a low-confidence investigation plan preserves the possible fix path without fabricating exact affected symbols.
initial_investigation: Read the complete live issue body, both comments, labels, assignees, and timeline.
Confirmed the author supplied a replacement diagnostic archive after the earlier automated request.
Checked recent public history for AlwaysOnTop.cpp; the current display-adjacent change addresses WM_ENDSESSION shutdown hangs rather than the reported display-stack BSOD.
No linked or cross-referenced public fix attempt was visible.

information_gaps.information: A current-build control reproduction and correlation of the replacement diagnostic archive with the display-state transition.
information_gaps.why_needed: Determines whether the issue persists in current code and identifies whether a specific Always On Top operation can be safely mitigated.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Use the maintainer reproduction procedure with Always On Top enabled and disabled, retaining logs and crash details from each run.

reproduce.title: Validate Always On Top during display reconfiguration
reproduce.version_requirement: Current PowerToys stable or current main build
prerequisites: A multi-monitor Windows system, preferably with two high-refresh DisplayPort displays
A test window available for normal pin and unpin validation
setup: Record the Windows build, display topology, graphics driver version, and PowerToys version.
Run one control session with Always On Top disabled.
Run a paired session with Always On Top enabled without pinning a window initially.
steps: Repeat sleep and wake, lock and display timeout, and one-monitor power-cycle transitions over multiple cycles.
During the enabled session, also pin and unpin the test window between transitions.
Retain PowerToys logs and any crash information for each enabled and disabled run.
reproduce.expected_result: The current build remains stable in both control and enabled sessions; any recurrence is correlated to the exact display transition and Always On Top state.
